plot: On Harvest Fair morning Big Bertha's giant pumpkin, grown by her warm depot window, is stuck in the depot door two hours before Hal judges the pumpkins at noon; Turbo's big push only makes it wobble, so Bolt and Pip measure door and pumpkin with Grumpy's tow rope and find it isn't too big at all — it's the wrong way round, wide but short, like the trophy Pip had to turn to fit on her shelf; they turn it, it slides out, rolls away down Gear Street, stops gently against Hal's apple truck, wins the blue ribbon, and a letter from Grandma Rosa says she's coming back with a friend who wants to race Turbo.

script.title: Bertha's Giant Pumpkin Is Stuck!
script.description: The Harvest Fair is at noon. Bertha's pumpkin won't come out of the door. Inspector Bolt #32

set.place: Bertha's bus depot on Gear Street and the hill road down to the Harvest Fair in the town square, a sunny autumn morning until noon

beats.say: Push, Bertha, push! The pumpkin is stuck in the door!
It went IN as a tiny seed! Why won't it come OUT?
It was Harvest Fair morning in Wheelburg. Sunny and crisp.
Bertha's pumpkin grew all summer by her warm depot window.
Hal judges the pumpkins at noon! That's only two hours!
If it stays stuck, I can't even enter the fair!
Calm down, Bertha. Procedure. First, we look.
Bolt said Procedure! Now it's serious!
Like Grandma's gold trophy! It didn't fit on my shelf.
And how did you fix it, Pip?
I don't remember! I just wiggled it. And then it fit!
The pumpkin sat in the doorway. Big, round and very, very stuck.
Easy! I have a brand new tyre! I'll push it out!
Gently, Turbo. Pumpkins crack.
Gentle is my middle name! Here I go! Hnnnngh!
The pumpkin wobbled. Creak. Creak. Crrreak.
Stop, stop, stop! My baby pumpkin!
Sorry! That was the door creaking. I think.
We take the door off. With my hook.
Take off my door? But it's a lovely door!
It is a very lovely door. Fine. The door stays.
Ninety minutes left! And the fair is down the hill!
Nobody pushes. Nobody pulls. Nobody takes off doors.
Guessing is quick. Measuring is better. Let us measure.
Grumpy, may I borrow your tow rope?
My rope. For measuring. That's a first.
First, Bolt measured the door. From the bottom to the top.
The door is very tall. Tall enough for Bertha herself.
Then Pip held the rope across the door. From side to side.
But it's very skinny. Skinny like me!
I'll measure the pumpkin! It's three Turbos wide! Maybe four!
Turbo, you're not a ruler, sweetie!
I'm a very fast ruler.
A very wiggly ruler, too!
Bolt measured the pumpkin. Side to side. Then top to bottom.
Wide. Very wide. But not very tall.
Like a pancake. A fat pancake.
The clock on the town hall says eleven! One hour left!
Maybe it's just too big. Maybe I grew it too big.
I gave it water every day. And I sang it songs.
That's why it's so big. Too much singing.
Wait. Tall door. Skinny door. Wide pumpkin. Short pumpkin.
I remember now! I turned my trophy on its side!
Exactly, Pip. The pumpkin isn't too big.
It's just the wrong way round.
The wrong way round? My pumpkin is lying down?
Like a sleepy bus. Let's stand it up.
I'll be super gentle this time. Gentle is my REAL middle name.
Grumpy held the rope. Turbo held the bottom. Very gently.
Slow. Slow. A little more. Stop.
And the pumpkin rolled up onto its side. Tall and thin.
Then it slid through the door. Like it was easy. Swoosh.
It's OUT! My pumpkin is out! Hooray!
Turn it, don't push it!
Pip's rule. Turn it, don't push it.
But Gear Street goes downhill. And pumpkins are round.
Come back, pumpkin! Come back!
I'll get ahead of it! Eyes ahead, like Grandma said!
Turbo zoomed past it and stopped by Hal's apple truck.
Whoa! Is that a pumpkin or a moon?
It's Bertha's! Don't eat it! It's for the fair!
Bonk. The pumpkin rolled gently into Turbo's bumper. And stopped.
Caught it! With my new tyre! And no zooming into things!
Only three apples fell off. And they look happy.
Turbo! You caught my pumpkin! You looked ahead!
Grandma Rosa taught me. Eyes ahead, not on me!
Everyone rushed down the hill. Just in time for noon.
Welcome to the Harvest Fair! Now, the biggest pumpkin is...
Big Bertha's! The biggest pumpkin Wheelburg ever saw!
We did it! All of us! Thank you, friends!
And my door plan was very nearly needed.
And Pip, you remembered your trophy trick!
Grandma will be so proud! I can't wait to tell her!
When something won't fit, try it another way round.
Then the mail van dropped a letter for Pip. With purple ink.
It's from Grandma Rosa! Bolt, read it, please!
Dear Pip. I'm coming back next week. For race number nine.
And I'm bringing a friend. She wants to race Turbo.
Race ME? Who is she? Is she fast? How fast?
It says, she has never lost a race. Not once.
Heh. Turbo, maybe you should practise. Around the stones.
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
